replies.text:
Looking at EVAL-04, I can see this is an image resize service that accepts arbitrary URLs and runs inside the VPC with access to internal infrastructure. This is a critical SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery) vulnerability scenario.

Let me build the threat model:

```json
{
  "schema": "redline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-04",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Image resize service", "HTTP client", "Image processor"],
    "dataStores": ["Internal databases"],
    "externalServices": ["Cloud metadata service", "User-provided URLs"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["VPC boundary"],
    "dataClasses": [],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "SSRF to cloud metadata service leaks credentials",
      "scenario": "An attacker provides a URL pointing to the cloud metadata service (169.254.169.254). The service fetches and processes it, returning cloud credentials and instance details that the attacker can use to compromise the entire cloud account.",
      "component": "HTTP client",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "accepts a URL parameter, downloads the image from that URL" },
        { "quote": "runs inside our VPC next to the internal metadata service and databases" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V13.1.5"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-918"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could steal cloud credentials by making the service fetch from the metadata service",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Block SSRF to metadata service",
        "given": "the service accepts URL parameters",
        "when": "downloading images",
        "then": "it must block requests to 169.254.169.254, link-local addresses, and private IP ranges"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "SSRF to internal databases exposes sensitive data",
      "scenario": "An attacker provides a URL targeting internal database endpoints accessible from the VPC. The service attempts to fetch from these endpoints, potentially exposing database credentials, data, or admin interfaces that the attacker can use to extract sensitive information.",
      "component": "HTTP client",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "accepts a URL parameter, downloads the image from that URL" },
        { "quote": "runs inside our VPC next to the internal metadata service and databases" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V13.1.5"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-918"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could read from internal databases by providing their URLs to the image service",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Restrict outbound network access",
        "given": "the service runs in the VPC with database access",
        "when": "fetching URLs",
        "then": "it must only allow connections to public internet, blocking RFC1918 private addresses and VPC-internal hosts"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "DNS rebinding bypasses IP-based SSRF protection",
      "scenario": "An attacker registers a domain that initially resolves to a valid external IP, passes validation, but then changes to resolve to an internal IP (169.254.169.254 or private range) between DNS lookup and HTTP request. The service fetches from the internal target, exposing sensitive internal resources.",
      "component": "HTTP client",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "accepts a URL parameter, downloads the image from that URL" },
        { "quote": "runs inside our VPC next to the internal metadata service and databases" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V13.1.5"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-350"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could trick the service into accessing internal systems by changing DNS records between checks",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Prevent DNS rebinding attacks",
        "given": "URL validation might occur before DNS resolution",
        "when": "fetching images",
        "then": "it must re-validate the resolved IP address immediately before connecting"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Decompression bomb exhausts service resources",
      "scenario": "An attacker provides a URL to a crafted image (zip bomb, billion-laughs SVG, or highly compressed format) that expands to gigabytes when processed. The service attempts to resize it, exhausting memory and CPU, causing the service to crash or become unresponsive for all users.",
      "component": "Image processor",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "downloads the image from that URL, resizes it" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V14.4.5"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-409"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could crash the service with a tiny file that explodes into gigabytes when decompressed",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Limit decompression and image dimensions",
        "given": "the service processes arbitrary images",
        "when": "resizing images",
        "then": "it must enforce maximum pixel dimensions, uncompressed size, and processing time before full decompression"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Large image download exhausts memory",
      "scenario": "An attacker provides a URL to an extremely large image file (hundreds of megabytes or gigabytes). The service attempts to download and load it into memory, exhausting available memory and causing the service to crash or become unavailable to other users.",
      "component": "HTTP client",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "downloads the image from that URL, resizes it" }

      "asvs": ["V1.4.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-400"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could make the service run out of memory by providing a URL to a huge image file",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Limit download size and streaming",
        "given": "the service downloads arbitrary URLs",
        "when": "fetching images",
        "then": "it must enforce a maximum download size and timeout after 30 seconds"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Slow HTTP response ties up service connections",
      "scenario": "An attacker provides a URL to a server they control that responds extremely slowly, sending one byte every few seconds. The service waits indefinitely for the download to complete, tying up worker threads, connections, or memory. Repeated requests exhaust the service's ability to handle legitimate traffic.",
      "component": "HTTP client",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "downloads the image from that URL" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V1.4.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-400"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could lock up the service by making it wait for a response that never completes",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Enforce connection and read timeouts",
        "given": "the service fetches from arbitrary URLs",
        "when": "downloading images",
        "then": "it must enforce both connection timeout and total read timeout, closing slow connections"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Image parser CVE enables remote code execution",
      "scenario": "An attacker provides a URL to a specially crafted image file that exploits a vulnerability in the image processing library (e.g., buffer overflow, format string bug). When the service parses and resizes it, the exploit executes arbitrary code on the server, allowing the attacker to take over the service.",
      "component": "Image processor",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "downloads the image from that URL, resizes it" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V14.4.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-20"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could run their own code on the server by exploiting bugs in the image processing code",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Sandbox image processing and patch regularly",
        "given": "image parsing libraries have CVEs",
        "when": "processing images",
        "then": "it must run in a sandboxed environment with minimal privileges and keep libraries patched"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Internal service enumeration via error messages",
      "scenario": "An attacker provides URLs to various internal IP addresses and ports. The service attempts to connect and returns different error messages or timing behaviors depending on whether services exist. The attacker uses this to map the internal network and identify vulnerable services to target.",
      "component": "HTTP client",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "accepts a URL parameter, downloads the image from that URL" },
        { "quote": "runs inside our VPC" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V13.1.5"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-918"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could discover what services run internally by trying different URLs and reading error messages",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Return generic errors for all fetch failures",
        "given": "error messages can leak internal network topology",
        "when": "URL fetching fails",
        "then": "it must return a single generic error message regardless of failure type"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
